zh: 1937年7月8日凌晨，秘密警察逮捕了奥西普·皮亚特尼茨基（Osip Piatnitsky）。皮亚特尼茨基是斯大林俄国最高级别的共产主义官员之一，被指控策划针对苏联国家的恐怖活动。十天后，他的妻子开始写日记。尤利娅·皮亚特尼茨卡娅（Julia Piatnitskaya）的日记以动人的细节记述了丈夫被捕的情形，以及突如其来、深深刺入她这位共产主义精英生活的苦难和悲痛。邻居和以前的朋友都因为她是“人民公敌”的妻子而躲避她；她失去了工程师的工作，她和两个年幼的孩子被听任命运摆布，既没有收入也没有财产。在绝望中，一个关于她丈夫的问题在她脑海中打转，并开始困扰她。“他是谁？”她在日记中写道。皮亚特尼茨基真的是他宣称的那种忠诚的共产党人吗？她最初倾向于相信他；毕竟，他们已经结婚十七年了。但这将意味着党错了。皮亚特尼茨卡娅打断了她的反思：“显然我不那样认为。显然皮亚特尼茨（Piatnitsa）从来不是职业革命家，而是一个职业流氓——间谍或挑衅者……这就是他那样生活的原因，总是那么克制和严厉。显然，他的灵魂并不安宁，他看不到任何其他出路，除了等待被揭穿，或者抓住机会跑掉，逃避惩罚。”

皮亚特尼茨基是奥西普的化名。他出生时名叫约瑟夫·塔尔希斯（Iosif Tarshis），在加入布尔什维克地下组织后改了名。这个名字源于俄语中表示星期五的词“piatnitsa”，是他的同志们给他起的，他们将他对革命事业的奉献比作星期五对主人鲁滨逊·克鲁索的忠诚。然而，尽管奥西普有这样的革命履历，被捕之后，尤利娅仍无法完全肯定地说出丈夫究竟是什么人。她想相信他的保证，即他的布尔什维克良知“像刚下的雪一样白”，但相信这一点就要去想“黑暗”和“邪恶”的念头。这些念头违背了官方指控，其逻辑引导她去质疑国家在斯大林统治下前进的方向。最终，这破坏了她作为苏联公民和共产主义战友共同体成员的身份。这种身份植根于与集体齐头并进并建设光辉未来的承诺，对尤利娅·皮亚特尼茨卡娅来说，这就是她生命的本质。
en: In the early morning hours of July 8, 1937, the secret police arrested Osip Piatnitsky. One of the highest-ranking Communist officials in Stalin’s Russia, Piatnitsky was charged with plotting terrorist acts against the Soviet state. Ten days later his wife began to keep a diary. In moving detail, Julia Piatnitskaya’s journal recounts the circumstances of her husband’s arrest and the hardship and grief that cut, suddenly and deeply, into her own life as a member of the Communist elite. Neighbors and former friends shunned her as the wife of an “enemy of the people”; she lost her job as an engineer, and she and her two young children were left to their fate, with neither income nor assets. In her despair, a question about her husband revolved in her mind and came to preoccupy her. “Who is he?” she wrote in the diary. Was Piatnitsky really the devoted Communist he had claimed to be? Her first inclination was to trust him; after all, they had been married for seventeen years. But this would mean that the party was at fault. Piatnitskaya cut her reflections short: “Obviously I don’t think that. Obviously Piatnitsa was never a professional revolutionary, but a professional scoundrel—a spy or provocateur . . . And that’s why he lived the way he did, and was always so reserved and stern. Obviously, his soul was not at peace and he did not see any other way out, except to wait to be exposed or grab an opportunity and run, escape punishment.”

Piatnitsky was Osip’s pseudonym. Born Iosif Tarshis, he had been renamed after joining the underground Bolshevik organization. Derived from piatnitsa, the Russian word for Friday, the name was given to him by his comrades, who likened his dedication to the revolutionary cause to Friday’s devotion to his master Robinson Crusoe. Yet in spite of these credentials, Julia felt unable in the wake of Osip’s arrest to state with full certainty who her husband was. She wanted to believe his assurances that his Bolshevik conscience was “as white as freshly fallen snow,” yet to believe this was to think “black” and “evil” thoughts. The logic of these thoughts, which contradicted the official charges, led her to question the direction in which the country was going under Stalin’s rule. Ultimately, it undermined her own identity as a Soviet citizen and a member of the fighting community of fellow Communists. This identity, grounded in the commitment to march with the collective and build the glorious future, was for Julia Piatnitskaya the essence of her life.

zh: 皮亚特尼茨卡娅日记的一页页记录着她的自发观点与她为了恢复其作为一个忠诚共产党人的世界观而付出的反思性劳动之间的斗争。日记是一种工具，让她可以释放那些有毒的想法，从而重新获得一个献身革命者那坚定且统一的声音。她的任务是“证明，不是为别人，而是为你自己……你的地位高于妻子，高于母亲。你将以此证明你是伟大苏联的公民。如果你没有力量做到这一点，那就见鬼去吧。”

像尤利娅·皮亚特尼茨卡娅日记这样最近才向学者开放的个人文件，挑战了西方对极权主义社会，特别是对作为极权主义典范的斯大林政权的观念。当思考斯大林俄国的自我表达时，我们认为国家剥夺了公民表达自我的能力，个人的真实想法和抱负只能在躲开国家侵入性目光的私人领域表达。我们认为苏联公民在其私人内核中与其呈现出来的“官方”形象有着本质区别。我们将这些人视为自由主义主体：追求自主、珍惜隐私并将其视为自由自决领域的个人。在这种观点中，鉴于苏联国家摧毁其自主权和隐私的决心，苏联公民必然站在国家的对立面。

在理想形式下，日记被想象成一个以自发和非强迫方式表达私人信念的容器。鉴于极权体制中无处不在的国家压制，只有出于良知或对后世的关切、不同寻常的人，才会冒险秘密写日记。在乔治·奥威尔的小说《1984》中，温斯顿·史密斯开始写日记，目的是在反抗“老大哥”国家的过程中表达自我。写日记是一种违规行为，如果被发现，“几乎肯定”会“被处以死刑，或至少在劳改营服刑二十五年”。奥威尔的老大哥国家积极致力于废除任何个人自我的概念。强制性的集体生活形式剥夺了个人表达任何个人思想的时间、空间，甚至必要的工具——纸和笔。温斯顿·史密斯的日记是“一本特别漂亮的书”，“有着光滑的乳白色纸张，因年代久远而微微发黄……那是至少四十年来未曾制造过的种类”。他是在“城市贫民区一家肮脏的小旧货铺”买到它的。传达的信息很明确：个人日记——过去自由主义时代日常生活的一个事实——在极权国家没有立足之地。
在革命前的俄罗斯文化中繁荣发展的日记，被认为在革命后恐怖与互不信任的气氛中已经绝迹。那些在革命和苏联早期一直写日记的人，被认为在斯大林时代已经停止了书写，因为拥有个人文本很容易成为定罪的证据。
作家米哈伊尔·布尔加科夫的日记在1926年被秘密警察没收。在归还后（未对他提出指控），他销毁了它。

幸存的知识分子一致认为，日记在斯大林时期是一种不合时宜之物。利季娅·丘科夫斯卡娅在1938—1941年间以日记形式记录的与诗人安娜·阿赫玛托娃的谈话录序言中评论道，在那些日子里“甚至无法想象记一本真正的日记”。丘科夫斯卡娅补充说，她总是“省略或掩盖”她与诗人谈话的“主要内容”。在1967年写成的一份回忆录中，维尼亚明·卡维林回忆起20世纪30年代末在列宁格勒拜访他的作家同行尤里·特尼亚诺夫的情景。主人指着窗外，外面的空气中满是细灰，说道：“他们在焚烧记忆，他们已经这样做很久了，每晚都是……一想到每天晚上都有成千上万的人把日记扔进火里，我就要发疯了。”

然而，这种认为个人叙事普遍且统一受到压制的观点，现在正被从最近开放的苏联档案馆中涌现出的苏维埃政权最初几十年的大量个人文件——日记、信件、自传、诗歌——所反驳。日记在事实上似乎是该时期，特别是斯大林统治时期的流行流派。日记作者包括作家和艺术家，以及工程师和科学家、教师、大学教授和学生、工人、农民、国家行政雇员、党务工作者和共青团活动家、士兵、学童和家庭主妇。其中有各级党员，也有非共产党员，包括被定罪为政治反革命的人。
en: The pages of Piatnitskaya’s diary document the struggle between her spontaneous views and the reflective labor she applied to restore her worldview as a committed Communist. The diary served as a tool by which she could release her poisonous thoughts and thereby regain the assured and unified voice of a devoted revolutionary. Her task was to “prove, not for others, but for yourself . . . that you stand higher than a wife, and higher than a mother. You will prove with this that you are a citizen of the Great Soviet Union. And if you don’t have the strength to do this, then to the devil with you.”

Personal documents such as Julia Piatnitskaya’s diary, made available to scholars only recently, challenge the Western notion of totalitarian societies and particularly of the Stalinist regime, which stands out as totalitarianism’s paradigmatic case. When thinking about self-expression in Stalin’s Russia we think that the state denied its citizens the ability to express themselves, and that individuals’ true thoughts and aspirations were voiced only in private realms, shielded from the intrusive gaze of the state. We think that in their private core Soviet citizens differed qualitatively from the way they presented themselves “officially.” We see these people as liberal subjects: individuals in pursuit of autonomy who cherished privacy as a sphere of free self-determination. In this view, Soviet citizens surely stood in opposition to the Soviet state, given its determination to destroy their autonomy and privacy.

In its ideal form the diary is imagined as a receptacle for private convictions expressed in spontaneous and uncoerced fashion. Given the omnipresence of state repression in totalitarian systems, only exceptional persons risk keeping secret diaries, impelled by conscience or a concern for posterity. In George Orwell’s novel 1984, Winston Smith begins to keep a diary for the purpose of expressing his self in defiance of the Big Brother state. Keeping a diary is an infraction that, if detected, is “reasonably certain” to be “punished by death, or at least by twenty-five years in a forced-labor camp.” Orwell’s Big Brother state actively strives to abolish any notion of an individual self. Enforced collective forms of life deprive individuals of time, space, and even the necessary tools—paper and pencil—to articulate any personal thought. Winston Smith’s diary is “a peculiarly beautiful book,” with “smooth creamy paper, a little yellowed by age . . . of a kind that had not been manufactured for at least forty years past.” He had bought it in a “frowsy little junk shop in a slummy quarter of the town.” The message is clear: a personal diary—a fact of daily life in the bygone liberal age— has no place in a totalitarian state.

Diaries, which thrived in prerevolutionary Russian culture, were presumed to have become extinct in the postrevolutionary climate of terror and distrust. Those who kept their journals through the revolution and the early Soviet years were thought to have ceased to do so in the Stalin era, when possession of a personal text could easily become self-incriminating.
The writer Mikhail Bulgakov had his diary confiscated by the secret police in 1926. After it was returned (no charges were brought against him), he destroyed it.

Surviving members of the intelligentsia concur that the diary was an anachronism in the Stalin period. It was impossible to “even conceive of keeping a real diary in those days,” Lydia Chukovskaya remarks in the preface to her conversations with the poet Anna Akhmatova, recorded in diary form in 1938–1941. Chukovskaya adds that she always “omitted or veiled” the “main content” of her conversations with the poet. In a memoir produced in 1967, Veniamin Kaverin remembered visiting his fellow writer Yuri Tynianov in Leningrad in the late 1930s. His host, pointing out the window where the air was filled with fine ash, said: “They are burning memory, they have been doing it for a long time, every night . . . I lose my mind when I think that every night thousands of people throw their diaries into the fire.”

Yet the notion of pervasive and uniform repression of personal narratives is countered now by a flood of personal documents from the first decades of Soviet power—diaries, letters, autobiographies, poems— which have emerged from the recently opened Soviet archives. Diaries in fact appear to have been a popular genre of the period, especially during Stalin’s reign. Diarists included writers and artists as well as engineers and scientists, teachers, university professors and students, workers, peasants, state administration employees, party workers and Komsomol activists, soldiers, schoolchildren, and housewives. Among them were party members of various ranks as well as non-Communists, including people convicted as political counterrevolutionaries.

zh: 他们的个人编年史描绘了一个以自我反思和斗争为特征的存在领域。许多苏联日记具有明显的内省色彩，但内省并非与个人主义目的挂钩。与温斯顿·史密斯那种将日记中的“我”转向反对国家宣传的目标和价值不同，这些苏联日记作者透露出一种强烈的冲动，要将自己写进他们的社会和政治秩序中。他们积极投身共同的革命事业，希望以此成为历史主体，实现自我。他们的个人叙事充满了苏联革命的价值观和范畴，以至于似乎消除了私人领域和公共领域之间的任何界限。许多斯大林时代的日记作者专注于弄清自己的本质以及如何改变自己。他们动笔书写是因为他们有着关于自身的紧迫问题，并试图在日记的自我拷问中寻找答案。日记是他们主动使用的工具，用来干预自身，使自己与革命时间的轴线相一致。
en: Their personal chronicles map an existential terrain marked by self-reflection and struggle. Many Soviet diaries were distinctly introspective, but introspection was not linked to individualist purposes. In contrast to Winston Smith, whose diaristic “I” turns against the goals and values propagated by the state, these Soviet diarists revealed an urge to write themselves into their social and political order. They sought to realize themselves as historical subjects defined by their active adherence to a revolutionary common cause. Their personal narratives were so filled with the values and categories of the Soviet revolution that they seemed to obliterate any distinction between a private and a public domain. Many Stalin-era diarists were preoccupied with finding out who they were in essence and how they could transform themselves. They put pen to paper because they had pressing problems about themselves and they sought answers in diaristic self-interrogation. Their diaries were active tools, deployed to intervene into their selves and align them on the axis of revolutionary time.

zh: 共产主义政权和这些苏联日记作者共同关注的自我转型，植根于1917年的革命，这场革命提倡将自我作为一个政治项目来重新思考。所有支持革命的政治参与者，无论其意识形态差异如何，都将其与根据理性、透明和纯洁的革命标准重塑社会生活及每个个体的目标联系在一起。人们期待已久的沙皇制度的覆灭，将开启一种开明的政治秩序，使俄罗斯摆脱农民大众身上所表现出的“黑暗”和迟钝顺从；正是这些特征造成了这个国家令人痛恨的落后。革命标志着区分旧生活与新生活的门槛。它指向一个由“历史规律”决定的完美未来，通过应用理性科学和现代技术，这个未来显得触手可及。这个未来被广泛想象为完美人类“新人”的栖息地，革命者将其描述为人体机器、不知疲倦的劳动者，或无拘无束、完整的“人格”。

创造“人类的改进版”（托洛茨基）是1917年10月夺权的布尔什维克政权的既定目标。重塑人类并创造人间天堂是共产主义运动存在的理由（raison d'être）。在向广大苏联民众宣扬这些目标的同时，每个共产党人都亲身肩负着一项使命：按照新人的形象改造自己的生活。共产党人迎接新世界的尝试，很大程度上表现为一场反对封建和资本主义社会“残余”的暴力斗争，因为这些残余滋生了自私和剥削的态度。与此同时，布尔什维克试图把民众转化为具有政治意识的公民，让他们拥抱历史必然性，并在理解和个人信念的基础上参与建设社会主义。通过大量的政治教育活动，苏联政权促使个人有意识地认同革命（按照党的领导层的解释），从而理解自己是历史戏剧的积极参与者。他们被要求将革命内化，并从客观历史进程以及主观自我的精神展开这两个方面去理解革命。
en: The concern with self-transformation, shared by the Communist regime and these Soviet diarists, was rooted in the revolution of 1917, which promoted a new thinking about the self as a political project. All political actors who sided with the revolution, whatever their ideological differences, linked it to the goal of remaking the life of society as well as of each individual according to revolutionary standards of rationality, transparency, and purity. The long-anticipated overthrow of the tsarist system was to inaugurate an enlightened political order that would deliver Russia from the “darkness” and sluggish acquiescence that characterized its peasant masses and lay at the core of the country’s cursed backwardness. The revolution marked the threshold separating the old from the new life. It pointed toward a perfect future dictated by the “laws of history,” a future that appeared within reach through the application of rationalist science and modern technology. This future was widely imagined as the habitat of a perfect human being, the “new man,” whom revolutionary actors described as a human machine, an untiring worker, or an unfettered, integrated “personality.”

To create an “improved edition of mankind” (Trotsky) was a stated goal of the Bolshevik regime that came to power in October 1917. To reforge humanity and create an earthly paradise was the raison d’être of the Communist movement. While preaching these goals to the Soviet population at large, each Communist personally lived under a mandate to transform his or her own life in the image of the new man. The Communist attempt to usher in the new world proceeded in great measure as a violent struggle against the “remnants” of feudal and capitalist society, which bred selfish and exploitative attitudes. At the same time, the Bolsheviks sought to transform the population into politically conscious citizens who would embrace historical necessity and become engaged in building socialism out of understanding and personal conviction. Through a multitude of political-education campaigns the Soviet regime prodded individuals to consciously identify with the revolution (as interpreted by the party leadership), and thereby to comprehend themselves as active participants in the drama of history. They were summoned to internalize the revolution and grant it an interpretation defined not only by the objective course of history but also by the spiritual unfolding of their subjective selves.

zh: 在斯大林统治下，该政权宣布要把社会主义新人变为现实。1928-1929年党内多数派做出的以极快速度实现国家工业化、实行农业集体化以及加强对所有阶级敌人的战争的决定，表达了摧毁“旧”世界残余并继续建设“新”世界的强烈愿望。斯大林政权认为革命已经成熟，并在其追随者中产生了新的意识，足以使这场进攻成为可能。工业化将为新人创造丰裕的物质栖息地。从极地飞行员到创纪录的采煤工和挤奶女工，斯大林时代的一系列英雄被表现为社会主义人格的化身。他们的英勇事迹展示了所有苏联公民可以而且事实上应该追求的目标，以证明自己作为人的潜能。斯大林时代推崇一种苏联梦，党内思想家尼古拉·布哈林在勾勒其轮廓时，隐然与个人主义的美国梦相竞争。在苏联梦中，社会主义将把受资本主义剥削压迫的没有灵魂的工人“转变为人，转变为集体的创造者和组织者，转变为自我精进的人，转变为自身‘命运’的有意识生产者，转变为自身未来的真正建筑师”。
在这些革命要求下，苏联公民根据其主观生活的轨迹受到评判。在强大的自我转型革命叙事与监控自我表达以窥探个体主观本质的政治监视体制这双重背景下，人们不能不意识到自己有责任拥有一份独特的“传记”，公开展示它，并努力实现自我完善。谈论和书写自己已成为极具政治色彩的活动。一个人的“传记”已成为具有相当政治分量的产物。
en: Under Stalin, the regime declared its intention to make the new socialist man a reality. The decisions in 1928—1929 by the party majority to industrialize the country at breakneck speed, to collectivize the peasantry, and to intensify the war against all class enemies, expressed a fervent desire to destroy all that was left of the “old” world and proceed with the construction of the “new” world. Stalin’s regime believed that the revolution had come of age and produced a new consciousness among its followers which would allow for this assault. Industrialization would create the rich material habitat of the new man. A panoply of Stalin-era heroes—from polar aviators to record-setting coal workers and milkmaids—was represented as embodying the socialist personality. Their heroic deeds demonstrated what all Soviet citizens could, and in fact should, aspire to, in order to justify their human potential. The Stalin era promoted a Soviet dream, the contours of which the party ideologist Nikolai Bukharin delineated in implicit rivalry with the individualist American dream. In the Soviet dream, socialism turned soulless workers, oppressed by capitalist exploitation, “into persons, into collective creators and organizers, into people who work on themselves, into conscious producers of their own ‘fate,’ into real architects of their own future.”

Under these revolutionary imperatives, Soviet citizens were judged upon the trajectories of their subjective lives. In the double context of potent revolutionary narratives of self-transformation and a regime of political surveillance that monitored self-expression for what it revealed about individuals’ subjective essence, people could not but be aware of their duty to possess a distinct “biography,” to present it publicly, and to work toward self-perfection. Talking and writing about oneself had become intensely politicized activities. One’s “biography” had become an artifact of considerable political weight.

zh: 对自我的思考与行动日益增多，引发了俄罗斯自传文学名副其实的爆发。不仅更多的人开始书写和谈论自己，而且自传领域触及了全新的人口阶层。这一过程导致作者在学习读写的同时，也在摸索自我表达的语言。

尽管如此，虽然共产主义政权在自传体证词的产生上投入了巨大精力，但这些声音并非只是在适应政权的利益。自我表述的语言并非源于一套预先定型的意识形态套话。相反，它繁荣于一个更大的革命生态系统中，共产主义政权既是其中的生产者，也是产物。对自我完善、社会活动以及与历史相协调的自我表达的承诺，早在俄国革命之前数十年就已存在；它植根于俄罗斯知识分子的传统。事实上，要配得上“知识分子”（intelligent）这一称号，就要表现出作为具有批判思维的历史主体的气质。这一19世纪的遗产塑造了1917年革命者的自我理解，并为追求社会身份和个人自我定义的政治提供了框架。

一些苏联革命者将日记与其他形式的自传实践一起视为自我反思和转型的媒介。然而，另一些人则带着不安和怀疑看待它，认为记日记本质上是一种“资产阶级”活动。一个共产党员是否适合写日记是一个有争议的问题。只要它有助于培养社会化的意识和行动意志，它就是合法的，但它也有可能滋生空谈，或者更糟的是，“哈姆雷特主义”——沉思冥想而非革命行动。在战友的注视之外独自写作的日记作者，面临着脱离滋养他们的集体的风险。如果不加约束，一位坚定同志的日记也可能变成反革命情绪的温床。绝非偶然的是，在搜查嫌疑“人民公敌”的住所时，日记是秘密警察最觊觎的材料之一。
en: The increased thinking about and acting on the self occasioned a veritable explosion of Russian autobiographical literature. It was not just that many more individuals began writing and talking about themselves but that the autobiographical domain reached entirely new layers of the population. This process led to authors groping for a language of self-expression at the same time as they learned to read and write.

And yet, while the Communist regime was heavily invested in the production of autobiographical testimony, these voices were not solely adapting to the regime’s interests. The language of self did not originate in a preformulated ideological litany. It thrived, rather, in a larger revolutionary ecosystem of which the Communist regime was as much a producer as a product. The commitment to self-improvement, social activism, and self-expression in concert with history predated the Russian revolution by many decades; it was rooted in the tradition of the Russian intelligentsia. In fact, to be worthy of the ascription intelligent was to show a disposition as a critically thinking subject of history. This nineteenth-century legacy shaped the self-understanding of revolutionary actors in 1917, and it provided the frame in which the politics of social identity and individual self-definition were pursued.

Some Soviet revolutionaries considered the diary, along with other forms of autobiographical practice, as a medium of self-reflection and transformation. Others, however, viewed it with unease and suspicion, believing diary-keeping to be an inherently “bourgeois” activity. It was a matter of dispute whether a diary befitted a Communist. It was legitimate as long as it helped develop a socialized consciousness and a will to action, but there was also the possibility that it could breed empty talk or, even worse, “Hamletism”—brooding thought instead of revolutionary action. Diarists writing on their own, outside their comrades’ gaze, risked cutting themselves off from the nurturing collective. Un-checked, the diary of a steadfast comrade could turn into a seedbed of counterrevolutionary sentiment. Not accidentally, diaries were among the materials most coveted by the secret police during searches of the premises of suspected “enemies of the people.”

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 21、22 页
zh: 因此，20世纪30年代的日记远非苏联国家培养革命意识政策的直接产物。只有在极少数情况下，日记才源于教室、编辑部或建筑工地明确布置的任务。在大多数情况下，这些记录是作者主动记下的，事实上，他们经常感叹缺乏据以塑造自己生活的准则：并没有官方公式说明如何清除“旧”的本质，又如何对正在形成的“新”本质保持信念。作为跨越时间的持续自我对话，日记显示了其他个人叙事所掩盖或压制的张力和裂痕。由于这个原因，日记为斯大林统治下自我表达的形式、可能性和极限提供了无与伦比的洞察力。诚然，并非这一时期的每一本日记都服务于内省目的或揭示了丰富的自我语言。但大量来自不同社会、世代和职业背景的日记作者，都在纠结于同样的问题：他们是谁，以及他们如何改变。他们的共同点是努力将自己的生活铭刻进革命事业的宏大叙事中。他们的记录显示了共同的自我表达形式与自我实现理想，这些共同性指向个别案例之外，暗示着更广泛的文化意义。
en: Thus the diaries of the 1930s are far more than unmediated products of Soviet state policies of fostering revolutionary consciousness. Only in a few cases did diaries originate as clear assignments prescribed in a classroom, an editorial bureau, or a construction site. For the most part, these records were kept on the initiative of their authors, who in fact often deplored the lack of guidelines according to which they could pattern their lives: there existed no official formula for how to purge oneself of an “old” essence and how to retain faith in an emerging new one. As an ongoing engagement with oneself through time, the diary showed tensions and fissures that other personal narratives glossed over or repressed. For this reason diaries yield unsurpassed in-sights into the forms, possibilities, and limits of self-expression under Stalin. To be sure, not every diary of this period served introspective purposes or revealed a rich language of self. But a great number of diarists, from a variety of social, generational, and occupational backgrounds, grappled with the same questions of who they were and how they could change. They held in common a striving to inscribe their life into a larger narrative of the revolutionary cause. Their records show shared forms of self-expression and ideals of self-realization, which point beyond the individual cases and suggest a wider cultural significance.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 22、23 页
zh: 这些日记的作者以鲜明的现代方式构思自己。米歇尔·福柯写道：“成为现代人，不是要在流逝的瞬息之流中接受本来的自己；而是要把自己当作复杂而艰难的自我塑造的对象。”
这意味着将自己理解为自己生活的主体——而不是把自己视作某种更高力量所安排的命运的对象。现代主体不再承认社会为他们预先规定的角色；他们寻求创造自己的个人传记。因此，主体性包含了一定程度的个体对塑造其生活的自觉参与。
更具体地说，我查阅的苏联日记提供了对非自由主义的社会主义主体性形成的见解。从19世纪作为一个政治运动诞生起，社会主义就被其追随者定义为自由资本主义的对立面。当苏联革命者着手建设社会主义社会时，他们与资本主义西方建立的工业现代性标准进行竞争。他们与后者一样致力于技术、理性和科学，但他们相信社会主义会在经济、道德和历史上胜出，因为它依赖于自觉的计划和有组织的集体的力量。
在这种背景下，自我叙事充实了社会主义作为一种反资本主义自我实现形式的含义和吸引力。日记作者构思了一种与资本主义西方相对立的理想生存形式，他们认为西方是个人主义的、自私的、狭隘的，一言以蔽之，是资产阶级的。他们努力达到一位日记作者所说的“第二阶段”的理解——一种逃离原子化存在并将自己理解为集体运动微粒的能力。
en: The authors of these diaries conceived of themselves in distinctly modern ways. “To be modern,” Michel Foucault writes, “is not to accept oneself as one is in the flux of the passing moments; it is to take oneself as object of a complex and difficult elaboration.”

It means to understand oneself as a subject over one’s own life—as opposed to comprehending oneself as, say, an object of higher fate. Modern subjects cease to recognize social roles predetermined for them; they seek to create their individual biographies. Subjectivity thus subsumes a degree of individuals’ conscious participation in the making of their lives.

More specifically, the Soviet diaries I have consulted provide insights into the making of an illiberal, socialist subjectivity. From its inception as a political movement in the nineteenth century, socialism was defined by its adherents in opposition to liberal capitalism. When Soviet revolutionaries proceeded to build a socialist society, they competed with a standard of industrial modernity established by the capitalist West. They shared with the latter a dedication to technology, rationality, and science, but they believed that socialism would win out, economically, morally, and historically, because of its reliance on conscious planning and the power of the organized collective.

In this context, self-narratives flesh out the meaning and appeal of socialism as an anticapitalist form of self-realization. Diarists conceived of an ideal form of existence in opposition to the capitalist West, which they perceived as individualist, selfish, narrow-minded, in a word, bourgeois. They worked toward what one diarist called a “second stage” of understanding—an ability to escape one’s atomized existence and comprehend oneself as a particle of a collective movement.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 23、24 页
zh: 更为广阔的集体生活被视为真正主体性的源泉。它许诺了活力、历史意义和道德价值，因而被人强烈渴求。相比之下，脱离集体或历史潮流的生活，由于无法参与苏联人民向前冲锋的生活，存在着个人倒退的危险。尤利娅·皮亚特尼茨卡娅意识到了这种动态，她的日记反复流露出迫切渴望重返集体的心情。在丈夫被捕后失去工程师工作的她，整天泡在公共图书馆翻阅技术期刊：“我翻阅了三月份的《机械工程》。我活着的每一天都把我进一步向后推。新机器正在制造：车床、农具、地铁和桥梁用的机器等等……工程师们正在以新的方式提出组织和工具生产技术的问题。总的来说，毫无疑问，无论有多少‘绊脚石’，生活都在向前迈进。斯大林汽车厂（ZIS）那美妙的文化宫。我简直嫉妒死了：为什么我不在他们的集体中？”

属于集体并与历史步调一致，是一个以工作和奋斗为前提的条件，伴随着滑坡、失败和重新承诺。在不断要求“警惕”的背景下，像尤利娅·皮亚特尼茨卡娅这样的日记作者描述了她们无法达到所要求的思想和行为标准。对于如何将新兴社会主义社会的华丽官方描述与她们个人生活的灰色惨淡现实结合起来，她们提出了明显的疑问和困惑。但她们转而反对自己的观察，认为那是源于“意志薄弱”，并誓言要奋斗下去。在某种程度上，犹豫和怀疑对于自我修养是必不可少的，并产生了一种新的奋斗和前进动力，日记作者正是通过这种动力体验到自己意志的展开。
en: The enlarged life of the collective was seen as the source of true subjecthood. It promised vitality, historical meaning, and moral value, and it was intensely desired. By contrast, a life lived outside the collective or the flow of history carried a danger of personal regression stemming from the inability to participate in the forward-thrusting life of the Soviet people. Julia Piatnitskaya was aware of this dynamic, and her diary resonated with a desperate insistence to rejoin the collective. Having lost her job as an engineer after her husband’s arrest, she spent her days at the public library, leafing through technical journals: “I looked through the March issue of Mechanical Engineering. Every day that I live pushes me further back. New machines are being built: lathes, agricultural tools, machines for the Metro, for bridges, etc . . . Engineers are raising in new ways questions of organization and the technology of tool production. In general, there is no doubt that life is moving forward, regardless of any ‘spokes in the wheel.’ The wonderful Palace of Culture for the ZIS [car] factory. I’m downright envious: why aren’t I in their collective?”

To belong to the collective and be aligned with history was a condition predicated on work and struggle, complete with lapses, failings, and renewed commitments. Against a background of incessant calls for “vigilance,” diarists like Julia Piatnitskaya described their inability to live up to the standards of thought and behavior required of them. They had pronounced questions and doubts about how to square glossy official representations of the emerging socialist society with the gray and dismal realities of their personal lives. But they turned against their own observations, which they believed to be born of a “weak will,” and vowed to struggle on. To an extent, hesitations and doubts were in-dispensable for the work on the self and produced a renewed dynamic of struggle and forward movement, the very dynamic through which diarists could experience the unfolding of their will.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 24 页
zh: 仅仅区分内心追求与外在顺从，已不足以理解苏联革命意识形态促使人自我改造和自我觉醒的力量。斯大林时代的许多个人叙事表明，意识形态是一种活生生的意义组织，人们会认真反思它。意识形态创造了张力，因为它往往与作者观察到的真相形成鲜明对比。然而，重点不在于关注张力点本身，而在于看个人如何化解它们：他们发现“双重灵魂”的状态多么难以忍受，退缩到私人生活对他们多么缺乏吸引力，以及他们如何运用合理化机制，试图恢复自己作为社会主义社会一部分的和谐自我观念。早期苏联体系中的许多意识形态张力并不存在于国家与公民（作为完全构成的自我）之间，而存在于公民与自身打交道的方式中。
en: A division between inner striving and outward compliance no longer suffices to understand the self-transformative and self-awakening power of Soviet revolutionary ideology. Many personal narratives from the Stalin era suggest that ideology was a living tissue of meaning that was seriously reflected upon. Ideology created tensions, as it often stood in marked contrast to an author’s observational truth. The point, however, is not to focus on the points of tension themselves but to see how individuals worked through them: how intolerable they found a condition of a “dual soul,” how little appeal a retreat into private life had to them, and how they applied mechanisms of rationalization in attempts to restore harmonious notions of themselves as part of socialist society. Much of the ideological tension in the early Soviet system did not exist between the state on the one hand and its citizens (as fully constituted selves) on the other, but in the ways citizens engaged their own selves.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 24、25 页
zh: 有一种广泛存在的倾向，是从字里行间解读斯大林时代的主体性，关注裂痕与沉默；与之相反，阅读应当从自传陈述的字面本身开始。研究极权主义主体证词多年的汉娜·阿伦特得出结论，“真正的理解几乎别无选择”，只能接受陈述表面所表达的内容：“史料在说话，它们揭示了行动着、并相信自己知道自己在做什么的人的自我理解与自我解释。如果我们剥夺他们这种能力，假装我们更了解并能告诉他们其真实的‘动机’是什么，或者他们客观上代表了哪些真实的‘趋势’——无论他们自己怎么想——我们就剥夺了他们说话的能力本身——只要言语是有意义的。”阿伦特总结道，除了那些罕见的、易于察觉的、人们有意识地撒谎的情况外，“自我理解和自我解释是所有分析和理解的基础。”
由于本书强调意识形态对斯大林时代主体生活的塑造力，它看起来可能是在向包括阿伦特和奥威尔在内的极权主义理论家回归。极权主义范式的信徒将共产主义领域的意识形态构思为源自中央国家机构并服务于政权利益的一套官方真理。意识形态向个人灌输观念，暗示他们参与了一场伟大的“运动”，而实际上却在他们真实的自由缺失状态上欺骗了他们。尽管这种解释在许多方面有说服力，但它把苏联公民贬低为政权抱负的纯粹受害者。
en: Against a widespread proclivity to read Stalin-era subjectivity between the lines and focus on cracks and silences, reading should begin with the very lines of autobiographical statements. Hannah Arendt, who studied the testimony of totalitarian subjects for many years, came to the conclusion that “true understanding has hardly any choice” but to accept statements as what they seem to express: “The sources talk and what they reveal is the self-understanding as well as the self-interpretation of people who act and who believe they know what they are doing. If we deny them this capacity and pretend that we know better and can tell them what their real ‘motives’ are or which real ‘trends’ they objectively represent—no matter what they themselves think—we have robbed them of the very faculty of speech, insofar as speech makes sense.” With the exception of those rare and easily detectable cases where people consciously tell lies, Arendt concludes, “self-understanding and self-interpretation are the very foundation of all analysis and understanding.”

With its emphasis on the shaping power of ideology over the lives of Stalin-era subjects, this book might appear to hark back to theorists of totalitarianism, including Arendt and Orwell. Adherents of the totalitarian paradigm conceive of ideology in the Communist realm as a corpus of official truths which issued from central state institutions and served the interests of the regime. Ideology indoctrinated individuals, suggesting to them participation in a great “movement,” while in fact deluding them about their true condition of unfreedom. Though in many ways compelling, this interpretation reduced Soviet citizens to mere victims of the regime’s aspirations.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 25、26 页
zh: 最近，一代社会历史学家揭示了大部分民众积极参与布尔什维克事业。在这一过程中，苏联秩序被奇怪地去意识形态化了，其运作被解释为被确定为其受益者的社会群体的“自身利益”。然而，这些历史学家并未尝试批判性地审视社会主义社会中自身利益可能采取的形式。
对这些立场的综合将为意识形态恢复名誉，同时保持一种个人能动感，这种能动性在本质上不是自主的，而是由意识形态产生的，并与意识形态动态互动。这种对意识形态和主体性作为交织和互动实体的关注，能更好地把握那个时代关乎生存的利害，除阿伦特外，极权主义理论家和修正主义者对此都不感兴趣。

意识形态与其说是一个给定的、固定的、独白式的文本语料库（如“共产党意识形态”），不如说是一种在个人体内起作用的发酵剂，在与特定个人的主观生活互动时产生大量的变化。个人就像一个交换场所，意识形态在那里被拆解和个性化，在这一过程中，个人将自己重塑为一个具有独特且有意义的传记特征的主体。而在激活个人的过程中，意识形态本身也获得了生命。因此，意识形态应被视为一种活的、适应性的力量；只有当它在以意识形态主体身份与自我和世界打交道的活人身上发挥作用时，它才拥有力量。转型（社会空间和自我的转型）、集体化（个人主义生产者和自我的集体化）以及净化（政治肃反运动和个人自我完善的行为）这些革命宏大叙事的大部分逻辑，都是由苏联公民提供并再生产的：他们不断为令人费解的国家政策寻求合理解释，因而成为与党和国家领导人同样参与其中的意识形态行动者。
en: More recently, a generation of social historians revealed the active participation of large segments of the population in the Bolshevik enterprise. In the process the Soviet order was strangely de-ideologized and its workings were explained in terms of the “self-interests” of the groups in society that were identified as its beneficiaries. Yet these historians made no attempt to critically examine the forms self-interest could take in a socialist society.

A synthesis of these positions would rehabilitate ideology and at the same time maintain a sense of individual agency, agency that is not autonomous in nature but is produced by, and dynamically interacts with, ideology. Such attention to ideology and subjectivity as inter-twined and interacting entities provides a better sense of the existential stakes of the times, something that, with the exception of Arendt, neither totalitarian theorists nor revisionists were interested in.

Rather than a given, fixed, and monologic textual corpus, in the sense of “Communist party ideology,” ideology may be better understood as a ferment working in individuals and producing a great deal of variation as it interacts with the subjective life of a particular person. The individual operates like a clearing house where ideology is unpacked and personalized, and in the process the individual remakes himself into a subject with distinct and meaningful biographical features. And in activating the individual, ideology itself comes to life. Ideology should therefore be seen as a living and adaptive force; it has power only to the extent that it operates in living persons who engage their selves and the world as ideological subjects. Much of the logic of the revolutionary master narratives of transformation (transformation of social space and of the self), collectivization (collectivization of individualist producers and of the self), and purification (political purge campaigns and acts of personal self-improvement) was provided and reproduced by Soviet citizens who kept rationalizing unfathomable state policies and thus were ideological agents on a par with the leaders of party and state.

body.page: 原书 PDF 第 26 页
zh: 斯大林时代的日记作者对有目的、有意义生活的渴望，反映了一种普遍存在的将生活意识形态化的冲动，即将其转变为一种坚定的、内部一致的、总体化的世界观（Weltanschauung）的表达。这种对意义与社会归属的取向与布尔什维克重塑人类的努力相交汇。政权因此能够疏导那些在布尔什维克意识形态边界之外产生的、对自我肯定与超越的追求。从这个角度看，苏联项目表现为两次大战之间更广泛的欧洲现象的一个变体，这种现象可以被描述为一种双重义务：拥有个人世界观以及个人融入共同体。这种理想的存在形式被称为“对齐的生活”；它许诺了本真性与强烈的意义，通过履行历史或自然规律的集体行动来实现。
en: Stalin-era diarists’ desire for a purposeful and significant life reflected a widespread urge to ideologize one’s life, to turn it into the expression of a firm, internally consistent, totalizing Weltanschauung. This orientation toward meaning and social inclusion intersected with the Bolsheviks’ endeavor to remake mankind. The regime was thus able to channel strivings for self-validation and transcendence that emerged outside the ideological boundaries of Bolshevism. In this light, the Soviet project emerges as a variant of a larger European phenomenon of the interwar period that can be described as a twofold obligation, for a personal worldview and for the individual’s integration into a community. This ideal form of being was called an “aligned life”; it promised authenticity and intense meaning, to be realized in collective acts fulfilling the laws of history or nature.

zh: 对自我的诉求处于共产主义意识形态的核心。这是它的定义特征，也是它力量的巨大源泉。在一个根本层面上，这种意识形态充当了个人经验的创造者。任何将自己写入革命叙事的人，都获得了作为属于更大整体的个体行动者的声音。此外，在加入运动时，个人被鼓励去改造自己。共产主义诉求的力量不容低估，它承诺那些过去是奴隶的人可以将自己重塑为人类的典范。这种力量在文化程度较低的苏联公民摸索出的自传叙事中得到了令人心酸的表达，他们详述了自己从黑暗走向光明的旅程。苏联革命的普遍抱负与规模，将参与其中的个人提升到历史主体的水平，他在日常生活中推动历史朝着完美未来前进。我将讨论的许多日记都是在与共产主义项目那转型性和参与性的双重诉求的对话中产生的。
en: The appeal to the self lay at the core of Communist ideology. It was its defining feature and also a great source of its strength. On a fundamental level, this ideology worked as a creator of individual experience. Anyone who wrote himself into the revolutionary narrative acquired a voice as an individual agent belonging to a larger whole. Moreover, in joining the movement individuals were encouraged to transform themselves. The power of the Communist appeal, which promised that those who had been slaves in the past could remold themselves into exemplary members of humanity, cannot be overestimated. It is poignantly expressed in the groping autobiographical narratives of semi-literate Soviet citizens who detailed their journeys from darkness to light. The universal ambition and scope of the Soviet revolution raised the participating individual to the level of a historical subject who in his daily life helped implement history’s progression toward the perfect future. Many of the diaries I will discuss were produced in dialogue with the twofold, transformative and participatory, appeal of the Communist project.

zh: 《各各他：根据针对尤·伊·索科洛娃-皮亚特尼茨卡娅的第603号档案调查材料》（Golgofa: po materialam arkhivno-sledstvennogo dela No. 603 na Sokolovu-Piatnitskuiu Iu. I.），V. I. 皮亚特尼茨基编（圣彼得堡，1993年），第41页（1938年2月15日）。
en:
Golgofa: po materialam arkhivno-sledstvennogo dela No. 603 na Sokolovu-
Piatnitskuiu Iu. I., ed. V. I. Piatnitskii (St. Petersburg, 1993), 41 (2/15/
1938).

zh: 在谈到自由主义主体时，我指的是一种支撑西方自我观念的理论构建。公私区别对于建立在个人主体同意基础上的自由民主共同体观念至关重要。参见迈克尔·哈尔伯斯坦（Michael Halberstam）著，《极权主义与现代政治概念》（Totalitarianism and the Modern Conception of Politics）（纽黑文：耶鲁大学出版社，1999年），第46–49、113–117页。
en:
When speaking of liberal subjects, I refer to a theoretical construct
grounding Western conceptions of self. The private-public distinc-
tion is essential for the liberal democratic conception of a community
based on the consent of individual subjects. See Michael Halberstam,
Totalitarianism and the Modern Conception of Politics (New Haven: Yale
University Press, 1999), 46–49, 113–117.

zh: 乔治·奥威尔（George Orwell）著，《1984》（圣迭戈：哈考特·布雷斯·约万诺维奇出版社，1984年），第7–8页。
en:
George Orwell, 1984 (San Diego: Harcourt Brace Jovanovich, 1984), 7–
8.

zh: N. A. 博戈莫洛夫（N. A. Bogomolov）著，《20世纪初俄罗斯文化中的日记》（“Dnevniki v russkoi kul’ture nachala XX veka”），载《提尼亚诺夫文集：第四届提尼亚诺夫讲座》（Tynianovskii sbornik. Chetvertye tynianovskie chteniia）（里加：“大自然”出版社，1990年），第148–158页。乔治·尼瓦特（Georges Nivat）观察到，1917年之后，“日记作为一种私密写作体裁消失了。革命和恐怖都不利于它……新的人不再有内心世界。私人日记？他甚至不知道那意味着什么。”见乔治·尼瓦特著，《俄罗斯的私密日记》（“Le journal intime en Russie”），载于尼瓦特著，《俄罗斯-欧洲：分裂的终结：文学与政治研究》（Russie-Europe: la fin du schisme. Etudes littéraires et politiques）（洛桑：人的时代出版社，1993年），第146页。
en:
N. A. Bogomolov, “Dnevniki v russkoi kul’ture nachala XX veka,” in
Tynianovskii sbornik. Chetvertye tynianovskie chteniia (Riga: “Zinatne,”
1990), 148–158. After 1917, Georges Nivat observes, “the diary as a genre
of intimate writing disappears. Neither the revolution nor the terror
is favorable to it . . . The new man has no more interiority. A private
diary? He does not even know what that means.” George Nivat, “Le
journal intime en Russie,” in Nivat, Russie-Europe: la fin du schisme.
Etudes littéraires et politiques (Lausanne: L’age d’homme, 1993), 146.

zh: 布尔加科夫随后敦促他的妻子写日记，她也确实照做了：见叶琳娜·布尔加科娃（Elena Bulgakova）著，《叶琳娜·布尔加科娃日记》（Dnevnik Eleny Bulgakovoi）（莫斯科：书业出版社，1990年）。布尔加科夫的大部分日记以秘密警察制作的打字稿形式保存了下来。
en:
Bulgakov then urged his wife to keep a diary, and she did: Elena
Bulgakova, Dnevnik Eleny Bulgakovoi (Moscow: Izd-vo “Knizhnaia
palata,” 1990). Large portions of Bulgakov’s diary survived in the
form of a typewritten copy produced by the secret police.

zh: 莉迪亚·楚科夫斯卡娅（Lydia Chukovskaya）著，《阿赫玛托娃日记》（The Akhmatova Journals），第1卷：1938–1941（纽约：法拉尔、斯特劳斯与吉鲁出版社，1994年），第5页。但事实上，楚科夫斯卡娅在斯大林恐怖年代一直保持着几本日记。参见莉迪亚·楚科夫斯卡娅著，《死亡的这一边：1936–1976年日记选》（Po etu storonu smerti: iz dnevnika 1936–1976）（巴黎：基督教青年会出版社，1978年）；V. 卡维林（V. Kaverin）著，《结语：回忆录》（Epilog: memuary）（莫斯科：阿格拉夫出版社，1997年），第233页。
en:
Lydia Chukovskaya, The Akhmatova Journals, vol. 1: 1938–1941 (New
York: Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 1994), 5. In fact, however, Chukov-
skaia kept several diaries throughout the years of Stalin’s terror. See
Lidiia Chukovskaia, Po etu storonu smerti: iz dnevnika 1936–1976 (Paris:
YMCA-Press, 1978). V. Kaverin, Epilog: memuary (Moscow: Agraf, 1997),
233.

zh: 斯特凡·普拉根堡（Stefan Plaggenborg）著，《革命文化：十月革命与斯大林主义之间苏俄的人学观与文化实践》（Revolutionskultur. Menschenbilder und kulturelle Praxis in Sowjetrussland zwischen Oktoberrevolution und Stalinismus）（科隆：伯劳出版社，1996年）。在俄语中，“新的人”（novyi chelovek）一词虽然在语法上是阳性，但指的是一般意义上的人类，它代表了俄罗斯男人和女人都为之奋斗的理想。尽管如此，“新的人”具有明显的男性特征。
en:
Stefan Plaggenborg, Revolutionskultur. Menschenbilder und kulturelle
Praxis in Sowjetrussland zwischen Oktoberrevolution und Stalinismus (Co-
logne: Böhlau, 1996). In Russian the term “new man” (novyi chelovek),
while grammatically masculine, refers to humanity in a generic sense,
and it represented an ideal toward which both Russian men and
women strove. Nevertheless, the “new man” had distinctly male fea-
tures.

zh: 伊加尔·哈尔芬（Igal Halfin）著，《我灵魂中的恐怖》（Terror in My Soul）（马萨诸塞州剑桥：哈佛大学出版社，2003年）；奥列格·哈霍尔丁（Oleg Kharkhordin）著，《俄罗斯的集体与个人：实践研究》（The Collective and the Individual in Russia: A Study of Practices）（伯克利：加州大学出版社，1999年），第57–60页。
en:
Igal Halfin, Terror in My Soul (Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University
Press, 2003); Oleg Kharkhordin, The Collective and the Individual in Rus-
sia: A Study of Practices (Berkeley: University of California Press, 1999),
57–60.

zh: N. I. 布哈林（N. I. Bukharin）著，《布哈林狱中手稿》（Tiuremnye rukopisi N. I. Bukharina），第1卷：《社会主义及其文化》（Sotsializm i ego kul’tura）（莫斯科：“空中-XX”出版社，1996年），第66页。布哈林在1934年阐述了这些思想。见尼·布哈林著，《资本主义文化的危机与苏联的文化问题》（“Krizis kapitalisticheskoi kul’tury i problemy kul’tury v SSSR”），载《消息报》（Izvestiia），1934年3月6日、3月18日和3月30日。
en:
N. I. Bukharin, Tiuremnye rukopisi N. I. Bukharina, vol. 1: Sotsializm i ego
kul’tura (Moscow: “Airo-XX,” 1996), 66. Bukharin formulated these
ideas in 1934. N. Bukharin, “Krizis kapitalisticheskoi kul’tury i prob-
lemy kul’tury v SSSR,” Izvestiia, 3/6, 3/18, and 3/30/1934.

zh: 迈克尔·S. 戈勒姆（Michael S. Gorham）著，《用苏联方言说话：革命俄罗斯的语言文化与声音政治》（Speaking in Soviet Tongues: Language Culture and the Politics of Voice in Revolutionary Russia）（迪卡尔布：北伊利诺伊大学出版社，2003年）；叶夫根尼·多布连科（Evgeny Dobrenko）著，《国家作家的锻造：苏联文学文化的社会与美学起源》（The Making of the State Writer: Social and Aesthetic Origins of Soviet Literary Culture）（斯坦福：斯坦福大学出版社，2001年）。
en:
Michael S. Gorham, Speaking in Soviet Tongues: Language Culture and the
Politics of Voice in Revolutionary Russia (DeKalb: Northern Illinois Uni-
versity Press, 2003); Evgeny Dobrenko, The Making of the State Writer:
Social and Aesthetic Origins of Soviet Literary Culture (Stanford: Stanford
University Press, 2001).

zh: 尤其参见苏珊·莫里西（Susan Morrissey）著，《革命的先驱：俄罗斯学生与激进主义神话》（Heralds of Revolution: Russian Students and the Mythologies of Radicalism）（纽约：牛津大学出版社，1998年）；马克·斯坦伯格（Mark Steinberg）著，《无产阶级想象力：俄罗斯的自我、现代性与神圣性》（Proletarian Imagination: Self, Modernity, and the Sacred in Russia）（伊萨卡：康奈尔大学出版社，2002年）；玛丽娜·莫吉尔纳（Marina Mogil’ner）著，《地下人神话：20世纪初俄罗斯的激进微观世界作为符号学分析的对象》（Mif o podpol’nom cheloveke. Radikal’nyi mikrokosm v Rossii nachala XX veka kak predmet semioticheskogo analiza）（莫斯科：新文学评论出版社，1999年）。“生态系统”一词受卡特琳娜·克拉克（Katerina Clark）“革命生态学”概念的启发；见卡特琳娜·克拉克著，《彼得堡：革命的熔炉》（Petersburg: Crucible of Revolution）（马萨诸塞州剑桥：哈佛大学出版社，1995年），第1–29页；另见迈克尔·大卫-福克斯（Michael David-Fox）著，《思想的革命：1918–1929年布尔什维克的高等教育》（Revolution of the Mind: Higher Learning among the Bolsheviks, 1918–1929）（伊萨卡：康奈尔大学出版社，1997年），第190–191页。
en:
See esp. Susan Morrissey, Heralds of Revolution: Russian Students and the
Mythologies of Radicalism (New York: Oxford University Press, 1998);
Mark Steinberg, Proletarian Imagination: Self, Modernity, and the Sacred
in Russia (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 2002); Marina Mogil’ner,
Mif o podpol’nom cheloveke. Radikal’nyi mikrokosm v Rossii nachala XX
veka kak predmet semioticheskogo analiza (Moscow: Novoe literaturnoe
obozrenie, 1999). The term “ecosystem” is inspired by Katerina
Clark’s notion of an “ecology of revolution”; Katerina Clark, Peters-
burg: Crucible of Revolution (Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University
Press, 1995), 1–29; see also Michael David-Fox, Revolution of the Mind:
Higher Learning among the Bolsheviks, 1918–1929 (Ithaca: Cornell Univer-
sity Press, 1997), 190–191.

zh: 米歇尔·福柯（Michel Foucault）著，《什么是启蒙？》（“What Is Enlightenment?”），载《福柯读本》（The Foucault Reader），保罗·拉比诺（Paul Rabinow）编（纽约：万神殿出版社，1984年），第41页。尤里·洛特曼（Iurii Lotman）主张将现代自传文学解读为一种“行为计划文化”；见 Iu. M. 洛特曼著，《历史文化语境中的文学传记（文本与作者人格的类型学关系）》（“Literaturnaia biografiia v istoriko-kul’turnom kontekste. (K tipologicheskomu sootnosheniiu teksta i lichnosti avtora)”），载《洛特曼选集》（Izbrannye stat’i），第1卷（塔林：“亚历山德拉”出版社，1992年），第372页。
en:
Michel Foucault, “What Is Enlightenment?” in The Foucault Reader, ed.
Paul Rabinow (New York: Pantheon, 1984), 41. Iurii Lotman advocates
reading modern autobiographical literature as a “culture of program
of behavior”; Iu. M. Lotman, “Literaturnaia biografiia v istoriko-
kul’turnom kontekste. (K tipologicheskomu sootnosheniiu teksta i
lichnosti avtora),” in Lotman, Izbrannye stat’i, vol. 1 (Tallinn:
“Aleksandra,” 1992), 372.

zh: 虽然受到福柯著作的启发，但这种对主体性的理解并不是建立在福柯的“臣服”（assujetissement）概念之上的。他设计这个词是为了强调个人自主的幻象，从而批判自由主义的现代性；当应用于非自由主义的苏联国家时，它会产生问题。参见劳拉·恩格尔斯坦（Laura Engelstein）著，《混合欠发达：帝国与苏联时代的纪律与法律》（“Combined Underdevelopment: Discipline and the Law in Imperial and Soviet Russia”），载《福柯与历史写作》（Foucault and the Writing of History），简·戈德斯坦（Jan Goldstein）编（剑桥：布莱克威尔出版社，1994年）；简·普兰珀（Jan Plamper）著，《福柯的古拉格》（“Foucault’s Gulag”），载《批判》（Kritika）第3卷第2期（2002年）；约亨·赫尔贝克（Jochen Hellbeck）著，《苏联主体性实践分析：访〈帝国内〉编辑部》（“The Analysis of Soviet Subjectivity Practices: Interview with the Editors of Ab Imperio”），载《帝国内》（Ab Imperio），2002年第3期，第217–260、397–402页。关于福柯与主体性，见《福柯读本》；休伯特·L. 德莱福斯（Hubert L. Dreyfus）与保罗·拉比诺著，《米歇尔·福柯：超越结构主义与解释学》（Michel Foucault: Beyond Structuralism and Hermeneutics）（芝加哥：芝加哥大学出版社，1983年）。另见尼克·曼斯菲尔德（Nick Mansfield）著，《主体性：从弗洛伊德到哈拉维的自我理论》（Subjectivity: Theories of the Self from Freud to Haraway）（纽约：纽约大学出版社，2001年）。
en:
While inspired by the work of Foucault, this understanding of subjec-
tivity does not build on Foucault’s notion of assujetissement. He de-
vised this term to emphasize the illusion of individual autonomy, and
thus to critique liberal modernity; it poses problems when applied to
the illiberal Soviet state. See Laura Engelstein, “Combined Underde-
velopment: Discipline and the Law in Imperial and Soviet Russia,” in
Foucault and the Writing of History, ed. Jan Goldstein (Cambridge:
Blackwell, 1994); Jan Plamper, “Foucault’s Gulag,” Kritika 3, no. 2
(2002); Jochen Hellbeck, “The Analysis of Soviet Subjectivity Prac-
tices: Interview with the Editors of Ab Imperio,” Ab Imperio, 2002, no. 3,
217–260, 397–402. For Foucault and subjectivity, see The Foucault
Reader; Hubert L. Dreyfus and Paul Rabinow, Michel Foucault: Beyond
Structuralism and Hermeneutics (Chicago: Chicago University Press,
1983). See also Nick Mansfield, Subjectivity: Theories of the Self from Freud
to Haraway (New York: New York University Press, 2001).

zh: 参见斯蒂芬·科特金（Stephen Kotkin）著，《磁山：作为一种文明的斯大林主义》（Magnetic Mountain: Stalinism as a Civilization）（伯克利：加州大学出版社，1995年）；马丁·马里亚（Martin Malia）著，《苏联的悲剧：1917–1991年俄罗斯社会主义史》（The Soviet Tragedy: a History of Socialism in Russia, 1917–1991）（纽约：自由出版社，1994年）；《俄罗斯的现代性：政治、知识、实践》（Russian Modernity: Politics, Knowledge, Practices），大卫·L. 霍夫曼（David L. Hoffmann）与雅尼·科索尼斯（Yanni Kotsonis）编（纽约：圣马丁出版社，2000年）；大卫·L. 霍夫曼著，《斯大林主义价值观：1917–1941年苏联现代性的文化规范》（Stalinist Values: the Cultural Norms of Soviet Modernity, 1917–1941）（伊萨卡：康奈尔大学出版社，2003年）。
en:
See Stephen Kotkin, Magnetic Mountain: Stalinism as a Civilization
(Berkeley: University of California Press, 1995); Martin Malia, The So-
viet Tragedy: a History of Socialism in Russia, 1917–1991 (New York: Free
Press, 1994); Russian Modernity: Politics, Knowledge, Practices, ed. David L.
Hoffmann and Yanni Kotsonis (New York: St. Martin’s, 2000); David
L. Hoffmann, Stalinist Values: the Cultural Norms of Soviet Modernity,
1917–1941 (Ithaca: Cornell University Press, 2003).

zh: 汉娜·阿伦特（Hannah Arendt）著，《论极权主义的性质：一篇理解性的文章》（“On the Nature of Totalitarianism: An Essay in Understanding”），载阿伦特著，《理解论文集，1930–1954》（Essays in Understanding, 1930–1954）（纽约：哈考特·布雷斯出版社，1994年），第338–339页。
en:
Hannah Arendt, “On the Nature of Totalitarianism: An Essay in Un-
derstanding,” in Arendt, Essays in Understanding, 1930–1954 (New York:
New York: Harcourt, Brace, 1994), 338–339.

zh: 尤其参见希拉·菲茨帕特里克（Sheila Fitzpatrick）著，《苏联的教育与社会流动，1921–1934》（Education and Social Mobility in the Soviet Union, 1921–1934）（剑桥：剑桥大学出版社，1979年）；J. 阿奇·盖蒂（J. Arch Getty）著，《大清洗的起源：重新审视苏联共产党，1933–1937》（The Origins of the Great Purges: The Soviet Communist Party Reconsidered, 1933–1937）（剑桥：剑桥大学出版社，1985年）。
en:
See esp. Sheila Fitzpatrick, Education and Social Mobility in the Soviet
Union, 1921–1934 (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1979);
J. Arch Getty, The Origins of the Great Purges: The Soviet Communist Party
Reconsidered, 1933–1937 (Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1985).

zh: 一个例外是《磁山》，这是斯蒂芬·科特金（Stephen Kotkin）对马格尼托哥尔斯克市所做的精彩的微观历史研究，它启发了我自己的工作。在意识形态与主体性的关系上，我与阿伦特持有不同观点。阿伦特对作为主动主体的个人不感兴趣。对她来说，意识形态本身就是驱动力：“独立于一切经验”，意识形态在与个人的遭遇中消解了主体性。这种观点低估了个人在挪用意识形态过程中的主动和创造性参与，这一过程要求他们重新加工，而非放弃主观经验。见汉娜·阿伦特著，《极权主义的起源》（The Origins of Totalitarianism）（纽约：哈考特·布雷斯·约万诺维奇出版社，1979年），第470页。另见埃里克·奈曼（Eric Naiman）著，《公共场合的性：早期苏联意识形态的化身》（Sex in Public: The Incarnation of Early Soviet Ideology）（普林斯顿：普林斯顿大学出版社，1997年）。
en:
An exception is Magnetic Mountain, Stephen Kotkin’s superb micro-
history of the city of Magnitogorsk, which has inspired my own work.
I differ with Arendt on the relationship between ideology and subjec-
tivity. Arendt is not interested in the individual as an active subject.
For her, ideology itself is the driving force: “independent of all experi-
ence,” ideology eliminates subjectivity in its encounter with the indi-
vidual. This view underrates individuals’ active and creative participa-
tion in the appropriation of ideology, a process which asked them
to rework, rather than abandon, subjective experience. See Hannah
Arendt, The Origins of Totalitarianism (New York: Harcourt, Brace,
Jovanovich, 1979), 470. See also Eric Naiman, Sex in Public: The Incarna-
tion of Early Soviet Ideology (Princeton: Princeton University Press,
1997).
